## A product subflow and its replacement
A candidate consists of one root action, two second-level actions and four third-level actions. At each level the pair of displacement increments is exactly identical across the reached nodes, with exact barycentric probabilities. Its three increment directions span R3 and are individually J-null. Thus its eight final helper corners have the product of the three one-dimensional branch probabilities.

For a proposed extracted root mass theta, each of the seven old action flows is debited by theta times its exact conditional probability of reaching that node. The receipt checks every such debit against its currently available nonnegative flow. The removed seven-action subflow is internally conserved, has root outflow theta, and deposits exactly theta times the product probability at each of its eight final corners.

Replace it by a new root-to-corners arc realized by independent one-dimensional Brownian coordinates absorbed at the two prescribed coordinate endpoints, in the three null directions. The starting coordinate need not be the midpoint: its two exit probabilities are the exact original barycentric probabilities. Every corner is a strict-interior PSD helper; the entire auxiliary parallelepiped is inside the domain by convexity. The Brownian arc has exactly the SAME root outflow and eight incoming corner flows as the removed discrete subflow.

Therefore it preserves divergence at every node and leaves all original terminal stop flows untouched. The remaining ordinary action flows stay nonnegative; adding the Brownian arcs produces another finite acyclic Markov network with the identical actual terminal endpoint law. Sequential extractions are valid even when their time-space subtrees overlap: they debit only remaining OLD action flows, while previously added Brownian arcs remain present. No ancestry-disjointness assumption is needed for this pooled-flow construction. It is crucial that all shared action capacities are tracked exactly.
